Dated this the 10th day of April, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No2574/2007 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ernakulam is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 15.7.2007.

According to the petitioner, on 15.7.2007, while he was walking through Edakochi-Palluruthy road,
a KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KL- 15/4996 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit him down and as a result of which he sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner and the 2nd respondent is the driver of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.4,29,500/-
2025:KER:31546 limited to Rs.4,25,000/-.
4. The 1st respondent filed a written statement, admitting the accident, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A8 and C1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.2.26,080/- and directed respondents 1 and 2 to pay the same.
7. Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9. Heard Sri. T.R. Sugunan, the learned Counsel appearing for the 2025:KER:31546 petitioner/appellant, and Sri.Alex Antony Sebastian P.A., the learned Standing Counsel for the 2nd respondent/KSRTC.

sentences.text: The Point: In this case the accident is admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
As per the claim petition, the petitioner was conducting a CD shop, earning Rs. 3500/- per month.

The Tribunal also fixed his monthly income at Rs.3500/-.
11.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2007 will come to Rs.6000/-.Therefore, the learned counsel prayed for fixing the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.6000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

Since the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2007 will come to Rs.6000/-, in order to award just and reasonable compensation, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra),
2025:KER:31546 the notional income of the petitioner is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.6000/-.
12.

In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"lacerated wound on left ear and parieto occipital region and sub occipital region,
contusion on the right shoulder, multiple abrasion over the face and extremities and pain and tenderness of cervical spine.

CT scan of brain shows that he has sustained fracture on left frontal bone, involving anterior cranial base, both walls of sinus, left occipital bone, left maxilla, left frontal contusion, left high parietal SDH and brain oedema, CT scan of spine shows that C6-7 and C5-6 mild post. Disc bulge."

13. As per Exhibit C1 disability certificate issued by the medical board, the petitioner suffered 22%
permanent physical disability.
The Tribunal, has accepted the permanent physical disability of the petitioner as such and hence, I do not find any grounds to interfere with the same.
Therefore, the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is accepted as 22%, as fixed by the Tribunal.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 29 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 17, as held in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.3,76,992.
15.
Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.14,000/- being the income for 4 months @ Rs.3500/-.
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner might have lost income at least for a period of 6 months.

Therefore, towards 'loss of income' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.36000/-
(6000x 6 months).
16. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/-.
Towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.2000/- and towards transport to hospital Rs.1000/- was awarded.

sentences.text: the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' no 2025:KER:31546 compensation was awarded by the tribunal.
17. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 23 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'transportation expenses' and 'extra nourishment' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.50,000/-, Rs.2,000/- and Rs.5,000/- respectively.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life', petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/-.
18. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
19. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.5,41,992/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

20.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent Nos.1 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.5,41,992/- (Rupees five lakh fourty one thousand nine hundred and ninety two only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, excluding interest for a period of 702 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
21.On depositing the aforesaid amount
, the Tribunal shall disburse 2025:KER:31546 the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
